question: An aircraft is maintaining a 5.2% gradient is at 7 NM from the runway, on a flat terrain; its height is approximately:
explanation: Height = gradient × distance = 0.052 × 7 × 6 076 ft ≈ 2 210 ft.

question: An island appears 30° to the left of the centre line on an airborne weather radar display. What is the true bearing of the aircraft from the island if at the time of observation the aircraft was on a magnetic heading of 276° with the magnetic variation 12° W?
explanation: HDG(T) = 276 − 12 = 264°. Island is 30° left: bearing of island = 264 − 30 = 234°T. Aircraft from island = reciprocal = 054°T.

question: An aircraft is over position HO (55° 30N 060° 15W), where YYR VOR (53° 30N 060° 15W) can be received. The magnetic variation is 31° W at HO and 28° W at YYR. What is the radial from YYR?
explanation: HO is due north of YYR (same longitude), so the true bearing from YYR is 000°T. Radials use the variation at the station: 000 + 28 = 028°M.

question: An aircraft is cleared to enter Shanwick Oceanic Control Area at 56° N010° W. The VOR radials from TIR (N56° 29.6 W006° 52.6) and SLG (N54° 16.7 W008° 36.0) which will indicate this OCA entry point are:
explanation: True bearings: TIR → 56N 010W ≈ 255°T, SLG → 56N 010W ≈ 336°T. With about 8°W variation on the chart this gives radials ≈ 263° and 343°.

question: An aircraft is planned to fly from position A to position B, distance 320 NM, at an average GS of 180 kt. It departs A at 1200 UTC. After flying 70 NM along track from A, the aircraft is 3 MIN ahead of planned time. Using the actual GS experienced, what is the revised ETA at B?
explanation: Planned time for 70 NM = 23.3 min; actual 20.3 min → GS ≈ 207 kt. Remaining 250 NM / 207 = 72.6 min. 1200 + 20.3 + 72.6 ≈ 1333 UTC.

question: Given: Distance A to B is 90 NM, Fix obtained 60 NM along and 4 NM to the right of course. What heading alteration must be made to reach B?
explanation: 1-in-60: track error = 4/60 × 60 = 4°; closing angle = 4/30 × 60 = 8°. Alter heading 12° left.

question: An aircraft obtains a relative bearing of 315° from an NDB at 0830. At 0840 the relative bearing from the same position is 270° . Assuming no drift and a GS of 240 kt, what is the approximate range from the NDB at 0840?
explanation: Bearing changes from 45° on the nose-left to abeam (90°) — a 45° "doubling" case: range abeam = distance flown = 240 × 10/60 = 40 NM.

question: TT from A to B is 167° , and the distance is 140 NM. Variation is 12W at A and 14W at B You flight-plan WCA 8L. When the remaining distance to B is 35 NM you find that your position is 5 NM right of the flight plan track. Since over A you have steered as flight planned. What change of heading is required at this time to bring you directly to B?
explanation: Off-track 5 NM after 105 NM: TE = 5/105 × 60 ≈ 3°. Closing angle = 5/35 × 60 ≈ 8.6°. Total ≈ 11° left.

question: An aircraft at FL370 is required to commence descent when 100 NM from a DME facility and to cross the station at FL120. If the mean GS during the descent is 396 kt, the minimum rate of descent required is approximately:
explanation: Height to lose 25 000 ft. Time = 100 / 396 h = 15.15 min. ROD = 25 000 / 15.15 ≈ 1 650 ft/min.

question: A co-located VOR/DME is at 66° 42N 043° 15W where magnetic variation is 45° W and the transmitter aerial is 500 ft amsl. An aircraft flying at FL 330 is on the 225° radial and has a DME range of 10 nm; its position is:
explanation: Radial 225°M + 45W → 180°T, so the aircraft is due south. Slant range 10 NM at ~5.3 NM height → ground ≈ 8.4 NM → 66°42′ − 8′ ≈ 66°34′N, 043°15′W.

question: An aircraft is flying at FL 120, IAS 200 knots, temperature – 5° C, wind component 30 knots. At a position 100 nm from the next reporting point the aircraft is ordered to delay arrival by 5 minutes. The immediate reduction in IAS to comply with this request is:
explanation: TAS ≈ 240 kt; with 30 kt tailwind GS = 270 kt → 22.2 min for 100 NM. Adding 5 min requires GS ≈ 220 kt → TAS ≈ 190 kt, a 50 kt TAS cut ≈ 41 kt IAS.

question: You are on ILS 3° glideslope which passes over the runway threshold at 50 feet. Your DME range is 25 nm from the threshold. What is your height above the runway threshold elevation? (Use the 1 in 60 rule and 6000feet = 1 nautical mile)
explanation: 3° glide path ≈ 300 ft per NM (6 000 × 3/60). 25 NM × 300 = 7 500 ft + 50 ft TCH = 7 550 ft.

question: You are required to descend from FL 230 to FL 50 over a distance of 32 NM in 7 minutes. What is the required TAS when you expect WC-25 during the descent?
explanation: Required GS = 32 NM / 7 min = 274 kt. With a 25 kt headwind, TAS = 274 + 25 ≈ 300 kt.

question: TT from A to B is 167° , and the distance is 140 NM. Variation is 12W at A and 14W at B You flight-plan WCA 8L. When the remaining distance to B is 35 NM you notice that your position is 5 NM right of the flight plan track. Since over A you have steered as flight planned. What has the drift been since you were overhead A?
explanation: Track error = 5/105 → ≈ 2.7°. Drift was planned as 8° R (8° L WCA) plus 2.7° more = ≈ 10.8° R.

question: When flying from A to B, a distance of 120NM, you are 3nm left of track after 30NM. What is the required alteration of heading to make good B?
explanation: Track error = 3/30 × 60 = 6°; closing angle = 3/90 × 60 = 2°. Alter 8° right.

question: You are flying at a True Mach No of 0.82 in a SAT of -45° C. At 1000 hours you are 100 nm from the POL DME and your ETA at POL is 1012. ATC ask you to slow down to be at POL at 1016. What should your new TMN be if you reduce speed at 100 nm distance to:
explanation: LSS at −45 °C ≈ 588 kt → TAS ≈ 482 kt; planned GS = 100/12 min = 500 kt (18 kt tailwind). New GS = 100/16 min = 375 kt → TAS 357 kt → M 0.61.

question: An aircraft at 66° N 029° W obtains a bearing of 141° (relative) from an NDB at 64° N 022° W. The aircraft is heading 352° M and the variation is 15° W. The bearing to plot from the NDB on a Lamberts chart with a parallel of origin at 51° N is:
explanation: QDR at aircraft: 352 + 141 = 133°M → 118°T. Reciprocal 298°T measured at the aircraft. On the Lambert chart convergence = 7° × sin 51° ≈ 5.4°, so at the NDB the line plots as 298 + 5.4 ≈ 303.4°T.

question: An aircraft is heading north and its groundspeed is 120 knots. A radio beacon indicates a bearing of 085° on the RMI and 5 minutes later the bearing is 090° on the RMI. Using the 1 in 60 rule the approximate range of the aircraft from the radio beacon is:
explanation: Distance flown = 120 × 5/60 = 10 NM; bearing change 5°. Range = 10 × 60/5 = 120 NM.

question: TAS=240 knots. The relative bearing from an NDB is 315R at 1410. At 1420 the bearing has changed to 270R. What is your distance from the NDB at 1420?
explanation: Relative bearing changes 315 → 270 (45° to abeam): range abeam equals distance flown = 240 × 10/60 = 40 NM.

question: An aircraft is flying at FL 140 where the COAT is -5° C. It is flying at an indicated air speed of 260 kts and is experiencing a headwind of 34 knots. When 150 nm from the FIR boundary it is instructed to reduce speed in order to delay arrival at the boundary by 5 minutes. The required reduction in indicated air speed is:
explanation: TAS ≈ 323 kt; GS = 289 kt → 31.1 min for 150 NM. Adding 5 min needs GS ≈ 249 kt → TAS ≈ 283 kt; ≈ 40 kt TAS cut ≈ 33 kt IAS.

question: Given: Magnetic heading 311° Drift angle 10° left Relative bearing of NDB 270° What is the magnetic bearing of the NDB measured from the aircraft?
explanation: Magnetic bearing of NDB = MH + relative bearing = 311 + 270 = 581 − 360 = 221°M. (Drift does not enter — the bearing is from the aircraft's heading.)

question: You are flying a VFR route and have become uncertain of your position. Which is the best course of action?

options.text: Set heading towards a line feature - coastline, river, or motorway.
Turn round and fly your flight plan tracks in reverse until you see something you recognised before.
Fly a series of ever-expanding circles from your present position till you find your next check point.
Turn round and fly your flight plan in reverse back to base.

explanation: When uncertain of position, head for a large line feature (coast, river, motorway) that cannot be missed, then identify where you are on it.

question: Given: ILS GP angle = 3.5 DEG, GS = 150 kt. What is the approximate rate of descent?
explanation: ROD ≈ GS × glide angle × 100/60 ≈ 150 × 3.5 × 1.67 ≈ 875 ft/min (5 × GS for 3°, scaled to 3.5°).

question: What do you understand by the term white-out?

options.text: Flight conditions when you suddenly enter a cloud and all get white outside the cockpit windows.
When the terrain is covered with snow and the horizon blend with the sky, visual determination of height becoming difficult.
Taking off from a snow-covered lake.

explanation: White-out: snow-covered ground merges with an overcast sky, removing the horizon and surface definition, making height judgement very difficult.

question: An aircraft on a magnetic heading of 311° , drift 10° port (left), variation 10° E, measures a relative bearing to a NDB of 270° (rel.). What is the aircrafts QDM to the NDB?
explanation: QDM (magnetic bearing to the NDB) = MH + relative bearing = 311 + 270 − 360 = 221°.

question: Given: Distance A to B = 120 NM, After 30 NM aircraft is 3 NM to the left of course. What heading alteration should be made in order to arrive at point B?
explanation: TE = 3/30 × 60 = 6°; CA = 3/90 × 60 = 2°. Alter 8° right (aircraft is left of track).

question: What is the distance to touchdown when you are 670 ft QFE on a 3,2° glideslope approach?
explanation: Distance = height / (6 076 × tan 3.2°) = 670 / 340 ≈ 1.97 NM.

question: The ICAO definition of ETA is the:

options.text: actual time of arrival at a point or fix.
estimated time of arrival at destination.
estimated time of arrival at an en-route point or fix.

explanation: ETA (ICAO) refers to the estimated time of arrival at the destination (IAF for IFR, aerodrome for VFR).

question: You leave A to fly to B, 475 nm away, at 1000 hours. Your ETA at B is 1130. At 1040, you are 190 nm from A. What groundspeed is required to arrive on time at B?
explanation: 285 NM left with 50 min to go → GS = 285 × 60/50 = 342 kt.

question: The distance between two waypoints is 200 NM, To calculate compass heading, the pilot used 2° E magnetic variation instead of 2° W. Assuming that the forecast W/V applied, what will the off track distance be at the second waypoint?
explanation: Using 2°E instead of 2°W gives a 4° heading error → 200 × 4/60 ≈ 13–14 NM off track.

question: An aircraft at FL330 is required to commence descent when 65 NM from a VOR and to cross the VOR at FL100. The mean GS during the descent is 330 kt. What is the minimum rate of descent required?
explanation: Height to lose 23 000 ft; time = 65/330 h = 11.8 min → ROD ≈ 1 950 ft/min.

question: An aircraft at FL370, M0.86, OAT -44° C, headwind component 110 kt, is required to reduce speed in order to cross a reporting point 5 MIN later than planned. If the speed reduction were to be made 420 NM from the reporting point, what Mach Number is required?

An aircraft is at FL140 with an IAS of 210 and a true OAT of -5C. The wind component is -35 knots. When the aircraft is at 150 nm from a reporting point, ATC request the crew to lose 5 minutes by the time they get to the beacon. How much do they need?
explanation: TAS ≈ 262 kt, GS ≈ 227 kt → 39.6 min for 150 NM. +5 min → GS ≈ 202 kt; 25 kt TAS ≈ 20 kt IAS reduction.

question: An aircraft is at 5530N 03613W, where the variation is 15W. It is tuned to a VOR located at 5330N 03613W, where the variation is 12W. What VOR radial is the aircraft on?
explanation: Aircraft is due north of the VOR (000°T). Radial uses VOR variation 12°W → 012°.

question: (Refer to Jeppesen Manual chart E(LO)1) An aircraft is overhead MAC (N55° 25.8 W005° 39.0) at 1054 UTC. The aircraft is at FL270, COAT -40° C and the wind is 290° T/50 kts. In order for the aircraft to enter Shanwick Oceanic airspace at 56° N 010° W at 1114 UTC it should fly at a Mach No. of:
explanation: MAC → 56N 010W ≈ 151 NM on 285°T in 20 min → GS 453 kt. With 290/50 (≈ 50 kt headwind) TAS ≈ 500 kt; LSS at −40 °C ≈ 595 kt → M ≈ 0.84.

question: What is the definition of EAT?

options.text: Estimated time overhead the destination airfield.

explanation: EAT (Expected Approach Time): the time ATC expects the aircraft to leave the holding fix to commence the approach — effectively the initial approach fix time.

question: The relative bearing to a beacon is 270° R. Three minutes later, at a groundspeed of 180 knots, it has changed to 225° R. What was the distance of the closest point of approach of the aircraft to the beacon?
explanation: The beacon was abeam (270°R) at the start; 3 min later (9 NM flown) it is 45° behind. The abeam distance was the closest approach: 9 × tan 45° = 9 NM.

question: Radio bearings:

options.text: cut all meridians at the same angle.

explanation: Radio waves travel along great circles, so radio bearings are great-circle bearings.

question: Given: aircraft height 2500 FT, ILS GP angle 3° . At what approximate distance from THR can you expect to capture the GP?
explanation: 3° glide path ≈ 300 ft/NM: 2 500/300 ≈ 8.3 NM.

question: Given: An aircraft is flying a track of 255° (M), 2254 UTC, it crosses radial 360° from a VOR station, 2300 UTC, it crosses radial 330° from the same station. At 2300 UTC, the distance between the aircraft and the station is:

options.text: the same as it was at 2254 UTC.
greater than it was at 2254 UTC.
randomly different than it was at 2254 UTC.
less than it was at 2254 UTC.

explanation: Track 255°M is perpendicular to radial 345°; radials 360° and 330° are symmetric about it, so the range is the same at both times.

question: You are heading 345M, the variation is 20E, and you take a radar bearing of 30 left of the nose from an island. What bearing do you plot?
explanation: HDG(T) = 345 + 20 = 005°. Island 30° left → bearing 335°T from aircraft; plot from island 155°T.

question: An aircraft at FL350 is required to cross a VOR/DME facility at FL110 and to commence descent when 100 NM from the facility. If the mean GS for the descent is 335 kt, the minimum rate of descent required is:
explanation: Height to lose 24 000 ft; time = 100/335 h = 17.9 min → ≈ 1 340 ft/min.

question: An island is observed to be 15° to the left. The aircraft heading is 120° (M), variation 17° (W). The bearing ° (T) from the aircraft to the island is:
explanation: HDG(T) = 120 − 17 = 103°. Island 15° left → 088°T from the aircraft.

question: You are required to descend from FL 230 to FL 50 over a distance of 32 NM in 7 minutes. What will the glideslope be when you expect WC-25 during the descend?

A ground feature appears 30° to the left of the centre line of the CRT of an airborne weather radar. If the heading of the aircraft is 355° (M) and the magnetic variation is 15° East, the true bearing of the aircraft from the feature is:
explanation: HDG(T) = 355 + 15 = 010°. Feature 30° left → 340°T from aircraft; aircraft from feature = 160°T.

question: On a 12% glide slope, your groundspeed is 540 knots. What is your rate of descent?
explanation: ROD = GS (NM/min) × 6 076 × gradient = 9 × 6 076 × 0.12 ≈ 6 560 ft/min.

question: At 13:00 UTC an aircraft is on the 330° radial and 40 nm from a co-located VOR/DME. At 13:25 the aircraft is on the 020° radial and 40 nm from the same VOR/DME. If variation is 0° E/W how far has the aircraft travelled and what has been its track?
explanation: Two points 40 NM from the station 50° apart: chord = 2 × 40 × sin 25° ≈ 34 NM; direction perpendicular to the bisector 355° → 085°T.

question: A pilot receives the following signals from a VOR DME station: radial 180° +/- 1° , distance = 200 NM. What is the approximate error?

An aircraft is planned to fly from position A to position B, distance 250 NM at an average GS of 115 kt. It departs A at 0900 UTC. After flying 75 NM along track from A, the aircraft is 1.5 MIN behind planned time. Using the actual GS experienced, what is the revised ETA at B?
explanation: Planned 75 NM = 39.1 min; actual 40.6 min → GS ≈ 111 kt. 175 NM/111 kt ≈ 94.8 min → 0900 + 135 min ≈ 1115 UTC.

question: Given: TAS = 197 kt True course = 240° W/V = 180/30kt Descent is initiated at FL 220 and completed at FL 40. Distance to be covered during descent is 39 NM. What is the approximate rate of descent?
explanation: GS on 240° with 180/30 ≈ 180 kt → 39 NM ≈ 13 min. Height 18 000 ft → ≈ 1 400 ft/min.

question: An aircraft is descending down a 12% slope whilst maintaining a GS of 540 kt. The rate of descent of the aircraft is approximately:
explanation: ROD = 9 NM/min × 6 076 ft × 0.12 ≈ 6 560 ft/min ≈ 6 500 ft/min.

question: An aircraft at FL390 is required to descend to cross a DME facility at FL70. Maximum rate of descent is 2500 FT/MIN, mean GS during descent is 248 kt. What is the minimum range from the DME at which descent should commence?
explanation: Height 32 000 ft at 2 500 ft/min = 12.8 min. Distance = 12.8 × 248/60 ≈ 53 NM.

question: The distance between positions A and B is 180 NM. An aircraft departs position A and after having travelled 60 NM, its position is pinpointed 4 NM left of the intended track. Assuming no change in wind velocity, what alteration of heading must be made in order to arrive at position B?

A ground feature was observed on a relative bearing of 325° and five minutes later on a relative bearing of 280° . The aircraft heading was 165° (M), variation 25° W, drift 10° Right and GS 360 kt. When the relative bearing was 280° , the distance and true bearing of the aircraft from the feature was:
explanation: HDG(T) 140°, track 150°. Bearings of the feature: 105°T then 060°T. Flown 30 NM; angle at first fix 45°, at second 90° → range 30 NM. Aircraft from feature = 240°T.

question: Given: ETA to cross a meridian is 2100 UTC GS is 441 kt TAS is 491 kt At 2010 UTC, ATC requests a speed reduction to cross the meridian at 2105 UTC. The reduction to TAS will be approximately:
explanation: At 2010: 50 min to go at 441 kt = 367.5 NM. In 55 min → GS ≈ 401 kt: reduce ≈ 40 kt (TAS reduction ≈ GS reduction).

question: At 65 nm from a VOR you commence a descent from FL330 in order to arrive over the VOR at FL 100. Your mean groundspeed in the descent is 240 knots. What rate of descent is required?
explanation: Height 23 000 ft; time = 65/240 h = 16.25 min → ≈ 1 420 ft/min.

question: An aircraft at FL310, M0.83, temperature -30° C, is required to reduce speed in order to cross a reporting point five minutes later than planned. Assuming that a zero wind component remains unchanged, when 360 NM from the reporting point Mach Number should be reduced to:
explanation: LSS at −30 °C ≈ 607 kt → TAS ≈ 504 kt: 42.9 min for 360 NM. +5 min → TAS ≈ 451 kt → M ≈ 0.74.

question: An aircraft at FL120, IAS 200kt, OAT -5° and wind component +30kt, is required to reduce speed in order to cross a reporting point 5 MIN later than planned. Assuming flight conditions do not change, when 100 NM from the reporting point IAS should be reduced to:
explanation: TAS ≈ 240 kt, GS 270 kt → 22.2 min. +5 min → GS ≈ 221 kt → TAS ≈ 191 kt → IAS ≈ 159 kt.

question: An aircraft at FL140, IAS 210 kt, OAT -5° C and wind component minus 35 kt, is required to reduce speed in order to cross a reporting point 5 MIN later than planned. Assuming that flight conditions do not change, when 150 NM from the reporting point the IAS should be reduced by:
explanation: TAS ≈ 262 kt, GS ≈ 227 kt → 39.6 min. +5 min → GS ≈ 202 kt → ≈ 25 kt TAS ≈ 20 kt IAS reduction.

question: An island appears 45° to the right of the centre line on an airborne weather radar display. What is the true bearing of the aircraft from the island if at the time of observation the aircraft was on a magnetic heading (MH) of 215° with the magnetic variation (VAR) 21° W?
explanation: HDG(T) = 215 − 21 = 194°. Island 45° right → 239°T. Aircraft from island = 059°T.

question: At 0422 an aircraft at FL370, GS 320kt, is on the direct track to VOR X 185 NM distant. The aircraft is required to cross VOR X at FL80. For a mean rate of descent of 1800 FT/MIN at a mean GS of 232 kt, the latest time at which to commence descent is:
explanation: Descent: 29 000 ft at 1 800 ft/min = 16.1 min, covering 16.1 × 232/60 ≈ 62 NM. Cruise to TOD: 185 − 62 = 123 NM at 320 kt ≈ 23 min → 0445.

question: Given: Distance A to B is 325 NM, Planned GS 315 kt, ATD 1130 UTC, 1205 UTC - fix obtained 165 NM along track. What GS must be maintained from the fix in order to achieve planned ETA at B?
explanation: Planned ETA 1130 + 62 min = 1232. At 1205, 160 NM to go in 27 min → ≈ 355 kt.

question: An aircraft at FL350 is required to descend to cross a DME facility at FL80. Maximum rate of descent is 1800 FT/MIN and mean GS for descent is 276 kt. The minimum range from the DME at which descent should start is:
During a low level flight 2 parallel roads that are crossed at right angles by an aircraft. The time between these roads can be used to check the aircraft:
explanation: The known distance between parallel line features crossed at 90° gives groundspeed.

question: Assuming zero wind, what distance will be covered by an aircraft descending 15000 FT with a TAS of 320 kt and maintaining a rate of descent of 3000 FT/MIN?
At 1000 hours an aircraft is on the 310 radial from a VOR/DME, at 10 nautical miles range. At 1010 the radial and range are 040/10 nm. What is the aircrafts track and groundspeed?
explanation: Two positions 10 NM out on radials 90° apart: chord = 14.1 NM in 10 min → 85 kt; direction perpendicular to the bisector 355° → 085°.

question: An RMI indicates aircraft heading. To convert the RMI bearings of NDB’ s and VOR’ s to true bearings the correct combination for the application of magnetic variation is:

options.text: NDB: aircraft position VOR: aircraft position
NDB: beacon position VOR: beacon position
NDB: beacon position VOR: aircraft position
NDB: aircraft position VOR: beacon position

explanation: NDB bearings are measured at the aircraft (use aircraft variation, as heading is magnetic there); VOR radials are referenced at the beacon (beacon variation).

question: An aircraft at FL370 is required to commence descent at 120 NM from a VOR and to cross the facility at FL130. If the mean GS for the descent is 288 kt, the minimum rate of descent required is:
explanation: Height 24 000 ft; time = 120/288 h = 25 min → 960 ft/min.

question: An island is observed by weather radar to be 15° to the left. The aircraft heading is 120° (M) and the magnetic variation 17° W. What is the true bearing of the aircraft from the island?
explanation: HDG(T) = 103°; island bears 088°T. Aircraft from island = 268°T.

question: A ground feature was observed on a relative bearing of 315° and 3 MIN later on a relative bearing of 270° . The W/V is calm; aircraft GS 180 kt. What is the minimum distance between the aircraft and the ground feature?
explanation: 45° off the nose to abeam: abeam range = distance flown = 180 × 3/60 = 9 NM (the minimum distance).

question: At 0020 UTC an aircraft is crossing the 310° radial at 40 NM of a VOR/DME station. At 0035 UTC the radial is 040° and DME distance is 40 NM. Magnetic variation is zero. The true track and ground speed are:
explanation: Chord between radials 310° and 040° (90° apart) at 40 NM = 56.6 NM in 15 min → 226 kt, track 085°.

question: An aircraft is descending down a 6% glideslope whilst maintaining a groundspeed of 300 kt. The rate of descent is approximately:
explanation: ROD = GS in NM/min × 6 076 ft × gradient = 5 × 6 076 × 0.06 ≈ 1 820 ft/min. (Quick rule: ROD ≈ gradient% × GS → 6 × 300 = 1 800.)

question: Cruising altitude 9 500 ft, airport elevation 1 000 ft, rate of climb 500 ft/min, average TAS 135 kt, track 215°T, average W/V 290°/20 kt, variation 3°W, deviation −2°, fuel consumption 13 gal/h. Find the time, compass heading, distance and fuel used during the climb.
explanation: Climb 8 500 ft at 500 ft/min = 17 min. With 290/20 the heading is ≈ 223°T and GS ≈ 128 kt → 128 × 17/60 ≈ 36 NM. Fuel 13 × 17/60 ≈ 3.7 gal. Only option C has the right time, distance and fuel.

question: A flight is made from VOR A (51°N 001°W, variation 8°W) to VOR B (51°N 006°W, variation 9°W) along the great circle, maintaining the same radial from A. Drift is 7° starboard. What is the magnetic heading on departure?
explanation: GC from A: 270 + ½ × 5 × sin 51° ≈ 271.9°T → radial ≈ 280°M (A variation 8°W). With 7° starboard drift, heading = 280 − 7 = 273°M.
